findings.detail: A setup or check can start a descendant with start_new_session=True while leaving stdout or stderr inherited. When the step times out, terminate_group() cannot stop that descendant, and the following communicate() waits without a deadline for its inherited pipe to close. A long-running descendant therefore prevents restoration and final JSON publication despite the configured timeout. This recurs in round 1's timeout-evidence class: the same-group timeout now retains diagnostics, but this sibling leaves the result incomplete instead of recording the failed phase. Bound the final output collection so an inherited pipe cannot prevent reporting.
findings.evidence: command() captures both streams through pipes at lines 144–145. Its timeout handler signals only the original process group at line 151, then calls communicate() without a timeout at line 152. A descendant that starts a new session belongs to another process group and retains those pipe descriptors. The exception handler repeats the unbounded drain at line 155. All setup/check phases and patch commands share this helper. The timeout regression at tests/checked_plant_test.py:247 uses an ordinary same-group sleep, so it does not cover this case.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: detached descendants can prevent timeout evidence from being published
